public_rationale: Nebius announced a substantial dedicated-capacity agreement with Meta during the target quarter. That establishes an identified AI-capacity customer beyond OpenAI and Anthropic. It contradicts the categorical absence claim. It does not establish that industry-wide investment is proportionate or profitable. The surrounding acknowledgment of Meta makes the distinction between those readings material.
limitations: The decisive evidence establishes contracted demand, not completed delivery.
Meta's demand does not prove a broad customer base outside hyperscalers.
A narrower claim about insufficient demand to justify all investment remains unsettled.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data center demand does not exist outside Anthropic and OpenAI, so data center investment is speculative.

statement.excerpt: Anyone investing in data centers is building speculative capacity for demand that does not exist outside of Anthropic and OpenAI.

from_speaker: demand that does not exist outside of Anthropic and OpenAI
our_interpretation: Read data centers as AI data centers, following the surrounding discussion.
Read the firm absence claim as denying substantial identifiable demand independent of OpenAI and Anthropic. Trivial demonstrations would not suffice as counterexamples.
A signed, substantial capacity agreement for another company's own AI operations demonstrates demand; it does not prove every investment will earn an adequate return.
Exclude purchases made by intermediaries specifically for the two labs. Include hyperscalers' independent own-use demand.
Use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter with public reporting available before the post.

The context acknowledges Meta and hyperscalers, creating tension with the categorical sentence. A narrower claim about demand sufficient to justify the entire buildout is not equivalent to this absence claim.

criteria.contradiction_condition: A dated, substantial AI-capacity contract or deployment identifies an independent customer using capacity for purposes other than serving the two labs.
